uncited: This family addresses the optimization of volume rendering algorithms specifically designed for distributed memory architectures (multicomputers), where data is partitioned across multiple independent nodes.
It solves the problem of minimizing communication overhead and redundant computation while maintaining load balance across the network.

The core mechanism shared by all methods in this family is the reduction of total computational work (shading, resampling, compositing) and network traffic per frame, while preserving visual fidelity.
**Alpha Cut-off:** Preventing wasted shading, resampling, and compositing operations by terminating ray integration when opacity falls below a threshold.
**Adaptive Refinement:** Varying the computational effort per screen tile based on local complexity.
**Local Acceleration Structures:** Using local data structures (e.g., octrees) to speed up traversal.
Originated in the early 1990s with research into parallel volume rendering on multicomputer systems.
